## E. Glossary of Key Terms

**AM** — Additive Manufacturing; the broad category of layer-by-layer fabrication technologies.  
**Assure** — Velo3D's proprietary in-process quality monitoring and traceability software platform; increasingly required for aerospace and defense part certification.  
**AS9100D** — The international quality management standard for aviation, space, and defense manufacturers; required for most aerospace supply-chain qualification.  
**Buy American Act** — Federal statute requiring U.S. government procurement to prefer domestically manufactured goods; relevant to Velo3D's ITAR-controlled systems.  
**CRADA** — Cooperative Research and Development Agreement; a formal mechanism allowing federal laboratories to collaborate with private companies on shared R&D.  
**EBITDA** — Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization; management's preferred non-GAAP profitability metric.  
**Flow Developer** — Velo3D's open-parameter software module (launched December 2025) enabling customer-customized process parameter development.  
**GRCop-42** — A NASA-developed copper-chromium-niobium alloy optimized for rocket combustion chamber walls; qualified on Velo3D's Sapphire platform.  
**GVSC** — Ground Vehicle Systems Center; U.S. Army R&D organization; Velo3D achieved first-AM-vendor qualification under GVSC initiative.  
**IDIQ** — Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity; a federal contract vehicle establishing ceiling value and terms without specifying delivery schedules in advance.  
**Intelligent Fusion** — Velo3D's patented closed-loop process-control architecture combining non-contact recoating, melt-pool monitoring, and real-time laser parameter adjustment.  
**ITAR** — International Traffic in Arms Regulations; U.S. export-control framework governing defense-related hardware and technical data, including Velo3D's Sapphire systems and process IP.  
**JAMA** — Joint Additive Manufacturing Acceptability; the Defense Logistics Agency's structured pilot program to qualify AM parts for military supply chains.  
**LPBF** — Laser Powder Bed Fusion; the metal additive manufacturing process in which a high-power laser selectively melts successive layers of fine metal powder within an inert-atmosphere build chamber.  
**NADCAP** — National Aerospace and Defense Contractors Accreditation Program; a performance-based supplier audit program widely required by aerospace primes and the U.S. government.  
**NAVAIR** — Naval Air Systems Command; U.S. Navy organization responsible for development and procurement of aircraft, weapons, and related systems.  
**NAVSEA** — Naval Sea Systems Command; U.S. Navy organization responsible for ships and combat systems; relevant to the Bechtel Plant Machinery naval nuclear relationship.  
**OTA** — Other Transaction Authority; a flexible U.S. government contracting mechanism used to accelerate prototype and production agreements with non-traditional defense suppliers.  
**RPS** — Rapid Production Services; Velo3D's parts-as-a-service offering in which the company operates Sapphire systems and delivers finished metal components to customers.  
**SupportFree** — Velo3D's branded capability to print metal parts with overhangs as low as zero degrees and internal diameters up to 100 mm without support structures requiring post-process removal.

financials.key_finding:
Velo3D's financial narrative is one of dramatic ascent, catastrophic contraction, and tentative stabilization. The company reached a revenue peak of approximately $81 million in FY2022 on the back of strong hardware system sales heavily concentrated in SpaceX Raptor-engine production programs. FY2023 saw the start of an order normalization from SpaceX and deteriorating bookings momentum, producing a sharp revenue decline that the company had guided would reach $105–115 million but instead fell sharply in the second half. By FY2024, full-year revenue had contracted to approximately $41 million — roughly half the 2022 peak — prompting the company's auditors to raise substantial going-concern doubt: as of mid-2024, accumulated deficit exceeded $385 million and cash was approximately $3.2 million, insufficient to fund 12 months of operations. The December 2024 debt-for-equity exchange (cancelling $22.4 million in senior secured notes in exchange for 95% common equity ownership by Arrayed Notes Acquisition Corp.) resolved the most acute liquidity stress but did not immediately alter the operating-loss trajectory.

FY2025 revenue recovered modestly to $46 million, a 12 percent improvement, but full-year gross margin deteriorated to negative 16.1 percent (from negative 5.1 percent in FY2024), driven in part by a $7 million inventory write-off in Q4 2025 and product-mix headwinds. The company's adjusted EBITDA improved from negative $58.5 million in FY2024 to negative $33.3 million in FY2025, reflecting substantial reduction in operating expenses ($47.5 million in FY2025 versus $76.8 million in FY2024). Year-end 2025 cash was $39.0 million — restored by the debt-for-equity restructuring and the new equity raise — providing materially improved financial footing. Q1 2026 revenue of $13.8 million (up 48% year-over-year) with a 17.2 percent gross margin represents the first quarters of meaningful gross-profit generation and validates the company's guidance trajectory. The April 2026 $50 million registered direct equity offering further strengthened the balance sheet, though Q1 2026 ending cash of $16.6 million (after the proceeds had not yet fully landed) suggests the company is deploying capital aggressively. Management guidance for FY2026 calls for revenue of $60–70 million, gross margin exceeding 30 percent in H2 2026, and EBITDA positivity in H2 2026 — ambitions that, if realized, would represent a fundamental inflection in the business's financial trajectory.
structural_observations: REVENUE BASE AND TRAJECTORY: FY2022 was the revenue peak at ~$81 million; FY2023 saw significant decline from the original $105–115 million guidance as SpaceX orders normalized; FY2024 bottomed at ~$41 million with going-concern qualification; FY2025 recovered modestly to $46 million; Q1 2026 at $13.8 million (up 48% YoY) implies an annualized $55 million run-rate already above FY2025, and the $60–70 million FY2026 guidance requires continued sequential ramp through the year.

GROSS MARGIN PROGRESSION: Gross margins have been deeply negative through the restructuring period — FY2024: -5.1%; FY2025: -16.1% (distorted by Q4 2025 inventory write-off of $7 million); Q1 2026: +17.2%. The path to the company's 30%+ H2 2026 target requires continued reduction in hardware-unit cost of goods sold, increased RPS services mix (higher structural margin), and disciplined pricing on new system and service contracts. The Q4 2025 gross margin of -73.6% — driven entirely by the inventory write-off — should be treated as non-recurring; underlying gross economics at the Q1 2026 level are meaningfully better.

CAPITAL STRUCTURE POST-RESTRUCTURING: As of December 31, 2025, Velo3D had total assets of $105.3 million, cash and cash equivalents of $39.0 million, stockholders' equity of approximately $38.2 million, and an accumulated deficit of $498.1 million. By Q1 2026, the April 2026 $50 million equity offering and the $15 million debt-to-equity conversions had reduced total outstanding secured debt by approximately 70 percent to approximately $9 million. The capital structure is meaningfully less precarious than the near-insolvency of mid-2024 but the $498 million accumulated deficit and history of serial capital raises imply ongoing dilution risk.

FISCAL YEAR CADENCE AND SEASONALITY: Velo3D's fiscal year ends December 31. Revenue cadence has historically been back-half weighted due to system-delivery timing and customer capital-budget cycles. Q4 2025's revenue decline (down 25% to $9.4 million, partially attributed to a government-shutdown-related timing delay) illustrates how defense and government procurement timing creates lumpy quarterly patterns. The company's 2026 guidance implies strong sequential ramp from Q1's $13.8 million to an implied average of $16–19 million per quarter in Q2–Q4.

DEBT VS. EQUITY AND CONTROL CONCENTRATION: The December 2024 debt-for-equity exchange gave Arrayed Notes Acquisition Corp. — controlled by CEO Arun Jeldi — 95 percent of common stock, making Velo3D functionally a controlled company. The April 2026 registered direct offering of 3.57 million shares at ~$14.00/share raised $50 million gross but partially diluted the controlling position. Outstanding secured debt was reduced to approximately $9 million as of Q1 2026. The combination of controlling-shareholder concentration and a $50 million external capital raise creates governance and liquidity dynamics that the dossier should examine: does Jeldi's multi-entity operating structure create related-party conflicts, and is the $50 million sufficient to fund the capital-intensive RPS expansion (capex guided at $40–50 million in 2026)?

COMPARABLE PEERS: Direct public comparables are limited. EOS GmbH (Germany, private) is the largest metal LPBF OEM; Nikon SLM Solutions (Germany, now majority-owned by Nikon Corp.) competes in multi-laser LPBF; Trumpf (Germany, private) competes via TruPrint. Among smaller public or recently public U.S. peers, Desktop Metal (DM, now restructured through bankruptcy/acquisition) and Markforged (MKFG, taken private 2024 by One Equity Partners) are cautionary precedents for capital-light AM businesses that failed to achieve scale. Velo3D's market cap as of the frozen snapshot date is heavily dependent on stock price trajectory following the April 2026 raise; at $14.00/share times the enlarged share count (post-issuance), the market cap would be in the $1–2 billion range, implying a 15–25x EV/Revenue multiple on FY2026 guidance — typical of high-growth defense-tech hardware names but demanding given negative EBITDA.

MARKET CAP VOLATILITY AND PENNY-STOCK HISTORY: Between the SPAC listing in September 2021 at an implied valuation above $1.8 billion and the nadir of 2024, Velo3D's equity experienced one of the more severe de-rating cycles in the additive manufacturing sector. The company has issued shares at deeply dilutive prices across multiple capital raises; the NASDAQ uplisting in August 2025 and the December 2025 SpaceX/Anduril confirmation catalyzed a significant stock price recovery that made the April 2026 equity raise possible at what appears to be a materially higher price than the trough.

leadership.key_finding:
Velo3D's leadership as of the frozen snapshot date is the product of a complete top-to-bottom management overhaul completed between late 2023 and early 2026. Founder Benny Buller — the Israeli-American technologist who conceived the SupportFree Intelligent Fusion platform in 2014, guided the company through its SPAC listing in 2021, and grew revenue to $81 million in FY2022 — was removed by the board in late 2023 amid the revenue collapse and capital crisis. Brad Kreger served as CEO through the acute crisis period of 2024 before being replaced in December 2024 by Dr. Arun Jeldi, who simultaneously completed the debt-for-equity transaction that gave his Arrayed Additive entity 95 percent of Velo3D's common equity.

Jeldi, 44, is a serial entrepreneur in advanced materials manufacturing. He runs three other companies concurrently — Arrayed Additive (which controls Velo3D), Lite Magnesium Products (aerospace and automotive magnesium components), and Crown Magnesium (magnesium extraction) — a management structure that is highly unusual for a publicly traded manufacturer and that raises legitimate governance questions about time allocation and potential related-party conflicts. He has no prior experience in laser powder bed fusion specifically, though his materials-manufacturing background is relevant to the Velo3D operational challenge.

The CFO seat was filled in March 2026 by James Suva, 55, effective April 6, 2026. Suva brings an unusual hybrid resume: 21 years as a Managing Director at Citibank where he led global IT hardware and technology equity research (giving him deep capital-markets credibility and analyst relationships), followed by a stint as SVP and Treasurer at Cricut, Inc. (2023–2026). His appointment signals that Jeldi wants a CFO who can manage the investor-relations narrative and equity financing activities as much as internal financial controls — consistent with the company's ongoing capital-raise activity.

The five-member board is diverse in relevant expertise: Dr. Adrian Keppler brings deep additive manufacturing credibility (former CEO of EOS GmbH, the world's largest metal LPBF OEM; now heads AM Scalation consultancy and serves on advisory boards of multiple AM startups); Stefan Krause brings large-cap corporate finance and automotive electrification experience; Jason Lloyd brings direct U.S. Navy engineering credibility relevant to the Bechtel Plant Machinery and NAVAIR relationships; and Kenneth Thieneman brings infrastructure construction and clean-technology experience.
research_notes_for_writer: JELDI GOVERNANCE CONCENTRATION: The fact that Arun Jeldi controls Velo3D through Arrayed Additive while also running three other companies is the central governance risk of the new era. The chapter writer should examine: (1) Whether Velo3D's DEF 14A proxy filings disclose any related-party transactions between Velo3D and Arrayed Additive, Lite Magnesium, or Crown Magnesium; (2) Whether the board's independent directors — particularly Keppler and Krause, who have the most relevant industrial experience — have publicly commented on the governance structure; (3) How institutional investors who participated in the April 2026 equity raise view the controlling-shareholder concentration.

BENNY BULLER DEPARTURE CIRCUMSTANCES: The circumstances of founder removal in late 2023 are not fully documented in public filings. The chapter writer should search for any board resolutions, 8-K filings, or contemporaneous press coverage explaining the stated rationale. Key questions: Did the board initiate the removal or was it part of a debt-holder-driven restructuring; was there any severance or equity settlement; and does Buller retain any equity stake in the restructured company or any licensing relationship?

JAMES SUVA CFO — DEPTH OF OPERATIONAL EXPERIENCE: Suva's background is primarily as a sell-side equity analyst and treasury official, not as a CFO of a manufacturing company. The chapter writer should assess whether this is an intentional choice (i.e., the company prioritizes investor-relations and capital-markets expertise at CFO) or a governance gap. For a company targeting $40–50 million in capital expenditures in FY2026 and managing complex government contracts, a CFO with manufacturing cost-accounting depth would typically be preferred.

BOARD COMPOSITION AND EOS CONNECTION: Dr. Adrian Keppler's prior role as CEO of EOS GmbH — Velo3D's most formidable direct competitor in metal LPBF — creates an interesting dynamic. The chapter writer should examine whether there are any information-barrier or conflict disclosures in Velo3D's proxy materials related to Keppler's concurrent EOS advisory relationships and his role at AM Scalation, which may serve EOS-affiliated clients.

JASON LLOYD — NAVAL RELATIONSHIPS: Lloyd's background as former chief engineer at Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA) and his work on the USS Gerald R. Ford program give him relationships that directly overlap with Velo3D's Bechtel Plant Machinery and NAVAIR customer relationships. The chapter writer should examine whether Lloyd plays a formal business-development advisory role for Velo3D beyond his board duties, and whether any formal consulting or introduction arrangements exist.

CFO TRANSITION TIMING: The CFO appointment (effective April 6, 2026) came immediately after the $50 million equity offering closed in April 2026. The chapter writer should assess whether Suva was instrumental in structuring the offering (suggesting he was working informally before his official start date) or whether the sequence implies CFO capacity was a gap during the capital raise.

PREDECESSOR CEO BRAD KREGER — WHAT CHANGED: Kreger was appointed CEO in late 2023 and held the role through the debt-for-equity close in December 2024 — approximately 12 months. His tenure encompassed the SpaceX $8M licensing deal, the Q3 2024 revenue nadir, and the final negotiation of the Arrayed Notes transaction. The chapter writer should examine what strategic decisions Kreger made versus what was forced by creditors, and whether his departure was amicable or contentious.
